metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the designated synthetic amount/quantity sentinels (or the rule producing them) so the 'no amount matches real billing' assertion has concrete values to check.
evidence: 'a test asserting the amounts are the designated synthetic values'
the synthetic sentinel values themselves have no stated source/provenance
findings.finding: AC requires 'a test asserting the amounts are the designated synthetic values' and 'no committed fixture amount matches real billing', but the plan never states what the designated synthetic values are, so the executor cannot know which constants the test must assert.
findings.location: AC 'No committed fixture amount matches real billing' / 'a test asserting the amounts are the designated synthetic values'
scenarios: Executor invents synthetic amounts; the assertion test is self-referential and proves nothing about real-billing divergence
findings.suggested_fix: Pick recognizable sentinels (e.g. amounts ending in .00 / round quantities like 1000) and state them, then assert those exact constants.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the guard's skip-floor as a concrete value (e.g. actual spend < $X for the UTC day) or the rule that derives it, so the near-zero-day test is anchored to a defined boundary.
evidence: 'skips days whose actual spend is below a floor, where the ratio is dominated by rounding'
No numeric floor or unit (USD/day) is stated
findings.finding: The guard's skip 'floor' below which no warning fires is asserted qualitatively ('actual spend is below a floor, where the ratio is dominated by rounding') but no concrete floor value or derivation is stated, leaving the executor to invent the threshold.
findings.location: Approach / AC 'The guard skips days whose actual spend is below a floor'
scenarios: Executor picks an arbitrary floor; the near-zero-day test passes vacuously against whatever value they chose
findings.suggested_fix: Name a default floor (e.g. skip when Cost Explorer actual for the day is below $1.00) and have the near-zero test assert at that boundary.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the guard's behavior when its Cost Explorer call fails (surface an error/alert rather than swallow), so a monitoring gap is itself observable.
evidence: 'Add a daily guard comparing the ceiling estimate for a settled day against Cost Explorer for that same day'
No mention of CE-call error handling, timeout, or a failure signal for the guard itself
findings.finding: The guard adds a new daily external dependency (a Cost Explorer get_cost_and_usage call) whose own failure behavior is unspecified: no timeout/error-handling/observability is stated for when Cost Explorer is unavailable or returns an error on the guard path.
findings.location: Approach 'Add a daily guard comparing the ceiling estimate ... against Cost Explorer'
scenarios: Cost Explorer throttles or errors on the guard's daily run; the guard silently produces no warning and the invariant goes unmonitored
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC that the guard emits an operational log/metric (or SNS notice) on Cost Explorer failure instead of silently skipping.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the guard's failure-disposition when its own CE/CloudWatch reads fail (transient/retryable vs skip-with-log), distinct from the invariant-violation warning, so a throttled read cannot silently disable the monitor.
evidence: Plan: 'The guard only warns: it cannot attach or detach the deny policy, so a guard fault cannot cause an outage.' — this covers the guard's effect on the deny policy, but not the disposition when the guard's own CE/CloudWatch reads fail.
AC covers the invariant-violation warning and the near-zero floor skip, but no AC addresses a CE/CloudWatch read failure on the guard path.
findings.finding: The daily guard adds a new path that calls Cost Explorer and CloudWatch list_metrics, but the plan states the disposition only of the guard's effect on enforcement ('a guard fault cannot cause an outage') — it never states what disposition surfaces when the guard's OWN dependency calls fail (CE unreachable/throttled, list_metrics throttled): does the guard silently no-op, retry, or emit an error/warning distinct from the invariant-violation warning?
findings.location: Approach — 'Add a daily guard comparing the ceiling estimate ... The guard only warns'
scenarios: Cost Explorer returns a throttle/5xx on the guard's daily run: without a stated disposition, a transient CE failure could be swallowed silently (the invariant monitor stops running unnoticed) or misfire as a spurious invariant warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an acceptance criterion: on a CE or list_metrics read error the guard logs a distinct transient/retryable diagnostic and skips that day's comparison without emitting a false invariant warning; add a test driving a CE read failure.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the daily guard reuses the existing 5-minute tick (gated to run its settled-day comparison once per UTC day) or introduces new schedule/Lambda infrastructure, and justify any new schedule against the existing 'no second schedule is needed' design.
evidence: Plan says 'Add a daily guard comparing the ceiling estimate for a settled day against Cost Explorer for that same day' but never names where it runs.

infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:417-420 comment: 'This same rule performs the 00:00 UTC release, so no second schedule is needed.' — the existing design deliberately uses a single rate(5 minutes) rule.
handler.py already polls CE (via _ce_spend_today) and prices with CEILING, so the guard can reuse both rather than standing up parallel infra.
findings.finding: The daily guard's execution vehicle is unspecified; if implemented as a new EventBridge schedule + Lambda it duplicates scheduling infrastructure the existing design explicitly avoids, whereas the once-per-day settled-day check could ride the existing 5-minute tick.
findings.location: Approach §2 (daily guard) and AC 'A daily guard prices a settled day with CEILING and compares it against Cost Explorer for that same UTC day.'
scenarios: Author adds a separate daily aws_cloudwatch_event_rule + Lambda for the guard, doubling the schedule/permission/log-group surface for a once-daily warn-only check.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that the guard runs inside the existing bedrock-spend-cap tick, gated to execute its settled-day CE-vs-CEILING comparison at most once per UTC day, so no second EventBridge rule, Lambda, or log group is added.

findings.checklist_item: State the guard's durable hosting: whether it is a new Lambda (name it, plus its schedule, execution-role IAM scope, and log group/retention) or an added code path in the existing tick handler reusing its role and log group.
evidence: Approach says 'Add a daily guard comparing the ceiling estimate for a settled day against Cost Explorer', with no statement of where it runs or what resource hosts it.

The existing stack in infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf runs one Lambda on a rate(5 minutes) tick with a scoped role and a dedicated log group; a 'daily' cadence does not map onto the 5-minute tick without a stated mechanism.
ABSENCE: no AC or Approach text names a new aws_lambda_function / aws_cloudwatch_event_rule / execution role / log group for the guard, nor states it reuses the existing handler and role.
findings.finding: The daily invariant guard's durable hosting is unspecified: the plan does not state whether it is a new Lambda with its own schedule, execution role, and log group, or an added code path in the existing tick handler/role. This choice determines the guard's IAM surface (ce:GetCostAndUsage / cloudwatch metric reads), its observability ownership (log group, retention, any alarm), and its reproducibility-as-code.
findings.location: Approach — 'Add a daily guard...' / Acceptance Criteria lines 6–9
scenarios: Reviewer/operator cannot tell whether a new IAM role and its scope are being introduced, nor whether the guard's output/errors land in an owned, retained log group.
If the guard is a new scheduled resource, its schedule, role least-privilege, and log-group/retention are unreviewed durable infra.
